headline: Red Sox stink up Fenway while Bruins lock up Minten
morning_brew: That six to one loss at Fenway was a real stinker, a total disaster that I watched through my fingers like a bad horror movie. Patrick Sandoval fought through six innings but the bats just could not get anything going, leaving us with a frustrating result against a team sitting at the bottom of the division. Watching our offense go quiet on a night where we needed to keep the pressure on in the wild card hunt was tough to swallow. We had a total of four hits all night and that just isn't going to cut it when we are trying to solidify our spot in the bracket.

On the ice, the front office made a massive splash by signing Fraser Minten to a seven-year contract. Locking down a center like that for the long haul shows ownership is finally serious about building a core that can compete once we move past the recent transition years. It is a heavy investment, but seeing that kind of commitment to a young player is exactly what we need right now while the team resets for next season, and it is a nice bit of good news to wash down the taste of that baseball game.

We have to shake off last night and get back to work immediately with another game against Los Angeles tonight. I am going to put the frustration of the loss behind me and hope the lineup finds their rhythm under the lights. My neighbor Rick has a new theory that the grass at Fenway was cut unevenly last night, which is peak Rick, but I will be tuned in hoping for a much cleaner performance than what we saw yesterday.
